findings: With the physics refitted, the fit keeps only about a third of the observed column water at the edges (0.36), not the full convention.
The refit trades wet_sun down (2.01 -> 1.49) and convective_rain up (0.86 -> 1.04): less sunshine-driven land evaporation and more convective rain from the extra moisture.

Even refitted, observed edges leave land temperature ~1 % worse overall and arid regions 2.5 % worse in T. The interior-moisture gain in the Amazon does not outweigh the drier-interior temperature loss.
Conclusion: the southern-tropics warm bias is not mainly a lateral-boundary moisture deficit that a column-water edge can fix; the remaining error is internal (land-surface energy balance).
